findings.title: Plaintext password storage and comparison
findings.attack_path: addUser stores req.body.password verbatim and validateLogin compares with strict equality (fromDB === fromUser); bcrypt-nodejs is imported but the hashing/compare paths are commented out. Any read of the users collection (DB compromise, backup leak, NoSQL injection, or insider) exposes every credential in cleartext, enabling immediate account takeover and credential reuse against other services.

findings.title: Server-Side JavaScript injection via eval() on contribution inputs
findings.attack_path: handleContributionsUpdate runs eval(req.body.preTax/afterTax/roth) directly on attacker-controlled POST body. An authenticated user submits a payload (e.g. a process or require expression) that executes in the Node.js process context, yielding remote code execution, data exfiltration, or denial of service. isNaN validation runs only after eval has already executed.

findings.title: NoSQL injection via $where with unsanitized threshold
findings.attack_path: getByUserIdAndThreshold builds a Mongo $where clause by string-interpolating the raw query-string threshold into server-side JavaScript: {$where: `this.userId == ${parsedUserId} && this.stocks > '${threshold}'`}. An attacker supplies a threshold such as 0';while(true){}' (DoS) or 1'; return 1=='1 (auth-context data disclosure) to run arbitrary JS in the database engine and read all users' allocations.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery in research stock proxy
findings.attack_path: displayResearch concatenates req.query.url + req.query.symbol and passes it straight to needle.get with no allow-list or scheme check, then writes the response body back to the client. An authenticated user points url at http://169.254.169.254/ (cloud metadata), internal services, or file/gopher schemes to reach internal-only endpoints and exfiltrate the response.

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference on allocations endpoint
findings.attack_path: GET /allocations/:userId reads userId from the URL path (req.params) rather than the session, with only isLoggedIn enforced. Any authenticated user iterates :userId to view every other user's asset allocations and the joined name fields, a horizontal authorization bypass that is trivially automatable.

findings.title: Stored/reflected XSS from disabled template autoescaping
findings.attack_path: swig.setDefaults({autoescape:false}) globally disables output encoding. Profile fields and the shared memos board render attacker input unescaped ({{memo}}, {{firstName}} etc.). A memo or profile payload stored by a low-privileged user executes in any other viewer's session, including the admin's, stealing the (non-HttpOnly) session cookie and chaining to account takeover.

findings.title: Missing function-level access control on benefits (admin) endpoint
findings.attack_path: Routes for GET/POST /benefits are guarded only by isLoggedIn; the isAdmin middleware exists but the admin-gated registration is commented out. Any authenticated non-admin user lists all non-admin users and overwrites arbitrary users' benefitStartDate, a vertical privilege/function-level access bypass.

findings.title: Hardcoded session and crypto secrets in source
findings.attack_path: config/env/all.js ships literal cookieSecret 'session_cookie_secret_key_here' and cryptoKey 'a_secure_key_for_crypto_here'. Because the session-signing secret is public in the repo, an attacker forges/signs valid session cookies and impersonates any user (including admin), bypassing authentication entirely; the same applies to any data the static cryptoKey protects.

findings.title: Committed TLS RSA private key in repository
findings.attack_path: artifacts/cert/server.key is a real -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY----- committed alongside its certificate. Anyone with repo access (public OSS history, fork, or CI artifact) obtains the private key and can impersonate the TLS endpoint or decrypt traffic if this cert/key were ever reused in a real deployment.

findings.title: Default / seeded predictable credentials
findings.attack_path: db-reset.js seeds admin/Admin_123 and user1/User1_123, user2/User2_123 in plaintext and runs as Heroku postdeploy and docker-compose startup. Anyone who reads the public repo logs in as admin immediately, gaining full administrative access on every deployment that uses the default seed.

findings.title: Cleartext storage of regulated PII and financial data
findings.attack_path: ProfileDAO.updateUser persists ssn, dob, bankAcc, and bankRouting as plaintext (the encrypt/decrypt helpers are commented out). Any read of the users collection (via DB compromise, the NoSQL injection in TM-003, or backup exposure) discloses SSNs and bank details, triggering regulatory breach obligations.

findings.title: Missing CSRF protection on all state-changing routes
findings.attack_path: csurf is a dependency but app.use(csrf()) and the token-injection middleware are commented out in server.js, and no SameSite cookie attribute is set. An attacker hosts a page that auto-submits a forged POST to /profile, /contributions, /benefits, or /memos; a logged-in victim's browser sends the ambient session cookie and the request executes as the victim.

findings.title: Session cookie missing HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite and not regenerated on login
findings.attack_path: The express-session config leaves cookie HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite unset (all commented out) and handleLoginRequest sets req.session.userId without req.session.regenerate(). This enables session fixation (a pre-set SID survives login with elevated privileges) and lets XSS (TM-006) read the cookie via document.cookie, escalating to full account takeover.

findings.title: Application served over plaintext HTTP only
findings.attack_path: server.js starts http.createServer only (the https branch is commented out) and no HSTS/helmet is applied. Credentials, session cookies, SSN, and bank data traverse the network in cleartext, allowing a network-position attacker to sniff or man-in-the-middle the session and harvest regulated data.

findings.title: ReDoS via catastrophic-backtracking bankRouting regex
findings.attack_path: handleProfileUpdate validates bankRouting with /([0-9]+)+\#/, a nested-quantifier pattern vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking. An authenticated user submits a long all-digit string with no trailing # to pin a Node.js event-loop thread at 100% CPU, denying service to all users since Node is single-threaded.

findings.title: Open redirect on /learn
findings.attack_path: The /learn handler calls res.redirect(req.query.url) with no allow-list. An attacker crafts an app URL whose url parameter points to an attacker site; the trusted domain in the link lends credibility to a phishing/credential-harvesting flow after the redirect.

findings.title: Log injection / forging via unsanitized username in console logs
findings.attack_path: On a failed login, session.js logs the raw userName ('attempt to login with invalid user: ' + userName) with the CRLF-encoding fix commented out. An attacker injects newlines and forged log lines into the failed-login value to corrupt audit trails or hide subsequent malicious activity.

findings.title: Verbose error page leaks stack traces
findings.attack_path: errorHandler renders error-template with the full error object including err.stack and logs the stack to console. Any triggered error returns internal file paths, dependency versions, and code structure to the client, aiding reconnaissance for the injection and RCE findings above.

findings.title: Outdated and unmaintained dependencies (supply chain)
findings.attack_path: package.json pins mongodb ^2.1.18, swig ^1.4.2 (deprecated/unmaintained), marked 0.3.5 (multiple known ReDoS/XSS CVEs), and the runtime is node:12-alpine (EOL). A published exploit against any of these reaches the app over its normal request surface or via a poisoned transitive update, with no SCA gate in CI to catch it.

findings.title: Insecure CI/CD and container hardening (root container, no secret scanning)
findings.attack_path: The Dockerfile leaves the production privilege-drop/permission-hardening line commented out, docker-compose injects MONGODB_URI with no auth on Mongo, and CI (GitHub Actions/Travis) runs no dependency or secret scanning despite committed keys (D7) and hardcoded secrets (D8). A compromised dependency or build step runs with broad container privileges and the committed secrets are never flagged.

findings.title: MongoDB exposed without authentication
findings.attack_path: The Mongo connection string mongodb://mongo:27017/nodegoat (docker-compose / config) carries no credentials and the mongo service runs with no auth enabled. Any actor that reaches the database port reads or writes all collections (credentials, PII, financial data) directly, bypassing the application entirely.

findings.title: Username enumeration via distinct login error messages
findings.attack_path: handleLoginRequest returns 'Invalid username' vs 'Invalid password' as separate messages (the unified-message fix is commented out). An attacker enumerates valid usernames by observing which message is returned, then focuses credential-stuffing/brute-force (amplified by the weak password policy) on confirmed accounts.

findings.title: Weak password policy permits trivial credentials
findings.attack_path: validateSignup enforces only PASS_RE = /^.{1,20}$/ (the strong-policy regex is commented out) and there is no rate limiting or account lockout on /login. Users register one-character passwords and attackers brute-force or credential-stuff accounts unimpeded.

findings.title: Cross-context output encoding mismatch on profile website link
findings.attack_path: displayProfile HTML-encodes doc.website but the value is rendered into an href attribute context (<a href="{{firstNameSafeString}}">), the wrong encoding for a URL sink. A javascript: or data: URI bypasses the HTML encoding and executes script when the link is clicked, a stored XSS variant distinct from the autoescape gap.
